steps.title: Data Manager loads with all panels intact
steps.narration: We open the Data Manager page, which organises everything about your imported price history. All sections — Unfinished Imports, coverage table, and the fetch form — load cleanly with no errors.
steps.point_out: The 'Data Manager' heading, the Unfinished Imports panel showing its rows, and the fetch form are all visible without any blank boxes or error boundaries.

steps.title: Unfinished Imports panel shows paused and partial runs
steps.narration: The Unfinished Imports panel lists every import that didn't finish — partial runs and provider-paused jobs — so nothing is silently lost. Each row shows a plain-language status and action buttons.
steps.point_out: The rows in the Unfinished Imports panel with their status labels, Retry buttons, and Dismiss buttons are all visible and intact.

steps.title: Retry an unfinished import queues a new job
steps.narration: Clicking Retry on any unfinished import queues a fresh job attempt right away. The panel keeps all its rows — nothing disappears — and the job progress area updates to show the new job running.
steps.point_out: After clicking Retry, the Job progress panel shows a new running job while the Unfinished Imports panel still shows its full list of rows.

steps.title: Dismiss a row without losing the rest
steps.narration: Dismissing a row removes just that one entry and leaves every other row in place. The panel does not flash empty or lose its remaining imports.
steps.point_out: The dismissed row is gone and the row count drops by one, but the rest of the panel is unchanged and the section heading is still present.

steps.title: Exactly one global date selector — no accidental duplicates
steps.narration: A core design rule is that the whole product shares a single 'View as-of date' control. This iteration's fixes touched the Unfinished Imports panel and added no extra date inputs anywhere on the page.
steps.point_out: Only one date-related selector — labelled 'View as-of date' — is present on the page. The fetch form's start/end date fields are job-entry fields, not a second viewing-date control.

steps.title: Per-symbol coverage table confirms the dataset
steps.narration: Below the Unfinished Imports panel the per-symbol coverage table shows how many price bars each ticker has. This lets you see exactly where the data is healthy versus where more history is needed.
steps.point_out: The coverage rows listing each symbol alongside its bar count are visible. No raw JSON or 'Something went wrong' message appears anywhere on the page.
